clue.text: UV or IR deficiency - something bad for plants around

indicators.note: the plant trouble wraps itself around the word for deficiency, holding it in its middle

blocks.note: blight is a plant disease
a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: A gardener worries that plants lacking ultraviolet or infrared rays will suffer some blight.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash looks like it separates two items in a gardening note, and 'deficiency' seems to go with UV or IR; it belongs to the wordplay instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Black light is the name for radiation just outside the visible spectrum, such as ultraviolet, which the eye cannot see.

clue.text: Push out priggish person full of nonsense

indicators.note: a person full of something holds it inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a prude is prim and easily shocked
rot is rubbish talk

explanation.surface: Someone shoves out a prim, self-righteous person who talks drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out or thrust forward, so it is a verb matching push out.

clue.text: Tonight eat a fine, fancy, farinaceous suet-rich food - praised here incomprehensibly!

annotation.answer: FAIR FA FACE YOURHO NESTGR EATC HIEFT AINOTHEPU D DIN SONSIE-RACE

definitions.text: Tonight eat a fine, fancy, farinaceous suet-rich food - praised here incomprehensibly!

blocks.clueFragment: Tonight eat a fine, fancy, farinaceous suet-rich food
blocks.note: surface reading: an invitation to a hearty pudding dinner this evening
setter's reading: the famous opening lines of Burns's poem hailing the haggis, written in Scots most outsiders find baffling

explanation.surface: A menu writer gushes over tonight's heavy oatmeal-and-suet dish, praising it in words nobody can follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared for 25 January, Burns Night, when Scots eat haggis (oatmeal, suet and offal) and recite Robert Burns's 'Address to a Haggis', which opens with these lines.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the first two lines of the poem saluting the haggis as chief of all puddings, in broad Scots dialect.

clue.text: See 3
What killed King? Almost comic - a vegetable!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the comic's title loses its last letter

blocks.note: a cord such as a garrotte or bowstring, the strangler's weapon for doing away with a ruler
the Beano is a long-running British children's comic

explanation.surface: A murder-mystery question about a slain monarch, answered by a nearly comic revelation that the culprit was a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beano is a British weekly comic for children; dropping its O leaves BEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A string bean is the green bean eaten pod and all, a common garden vegetable.

clue.text: A home in which a father's set foot

indicators.note: in which tells us the home holds what follows inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a nest is a bird's home
a plus pa, a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Describes a house where Dad has finally put his foot down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': a father is set in the home. 'Foot' looks like part of the father's action, but it is the definition, in its poetry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse a foot is a rhythmic unit; an anapaest is the one with two unstressed syllables followed by a stressed one.

clue.text: See 3
Deal here known to Scots?

blocks.note: first meaning: Deal is a seaside town, so this is the county containing it
second meaning: Scots ken means know, and its past participle means known

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a transaction, but it is a town on the coast of south-east England, in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Kent is the English county where the town of Deal lies, and kent is the Scots word for known.

clue.text: Behave irresponsibly - day must have broken then?

blocks.note: first meaning: fool around
second meaning, read literally: when the dawn-singing bird is up and around, morning has come

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: the lark sings at dawn, so if it is about, day has broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is an informal idiom for messing around playfully instead of acting sensibly.

clue.text: Flair needed for picking ring for marriage?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a jocular sense: wedlock seen as a trap

indicators.note: picking up something means taking it in, so the ring goes inside

blocks.note: a nose for something is a flair for it
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A jeweller suggests you need real flair to choose a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring for marriage' sounds like a wedding band, but the ring is the letter O and marriage is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jokingly, marriage is called a noose, a tie that catches a bachelor and holds him tight.

clue.text: Rolls may be what one turns up with

definitions.text: Rolls may be what one turns up with

blocks.clueFragment: Rolls may be what one turns up with
blocks.note: surface reading: someone arriving in a Rolls-Royce car
setter's reading: bread rolls brought along to feed a function

explanation.surface: A wealthy guest arrives in style, driving a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes 'Rolls' look like the luxury car; it is the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who supplies food for parties and events would well arrive bringing bread rolls.

clue.text: Sum of money advanced was sufficient to have invoked admiration, they say

indicators.note: they say points to what people speak, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.clueFragment: was sufficient to have invoked admiration
blocks.note: to impress someone is to win their admiration

explanation.surface: A loan was large enough to win someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is a formal term for money advanced to someone, such as a float, for spending on official business.

clue.text: Praise a former racing champion

blocks.note: to laud is to praise
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to honour a retired motor-racing star.
explanation.definitionFit: Niki Lauda was an Austrian driver who won the Formula One world title three times.

clue.text: After month workers (with one chap extra) increased

blocks.note: AUG is the calendar abbreviation for August
men as in a workforce
Ted is a man's name, the one added fellow

explanation.surface: After a month, the workforce took on one more man and grew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets the order: the month comes first, then the workers, then the extra chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Augmented means made larger or added to, a past-tense verb just like increased.

clue.text: Ray's hidden explosive chemical compounds

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and reformed

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A man called Ray has stashed some dangerous explosive chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' suggests a word concealed in the clue, but here it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Anhydrides are substances formed by removing water from another compound, such as an acid, a class of chemicals.

clue.text: Persecutor of Christians having edict - a lion to be let loose

indicators.note: letting something loose frees it from its order, so the letters roam into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor issues a decree that a lion be released on the Christians.
explanation.definitionFit: Diocletian was the Roman emperor who launched the Great Persecution of the Christian church in AD 303.

clue.text: See 3
Greek character given name, male name with repeated word

blocks.note: tau is the Greek letter T
Tony is a man's first name
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man from Greece is given a name that repeats a word.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a tautonym is a scientific label whose genus and species parts are the same, such as Gorilla gorilla.

clue.text: One day to go round the equivalent of Mars? That seems quite possible

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so these letters enclose another

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
Ares is the Greek god matching Rome's war god Mars

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether one day a craft will orbit Mars, and another replies that seems likely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like the planet; it is the Roman god, whose Greek counterpart is Ares.
explanation.definitionFit: I dare say is a conversational phrase conceding that something is probably so, much like saying it seems possible.

clue.text: See 3
Longed for death, having got over battle

indicators.note: something that has got over another covers it, enclosing it

blocks.note: the end is death
to vie is to compete or fight

explanation.surface: A war-weary soldier who survived the battle yearns for death.
explanation.definitionFit: To have envied something is to have wanted, coveted or desired what someone else possessed.

clue.text: Knight in voyage that isn't quick

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a creature famous for slowness

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for a sea trip

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight
a sail is a trip by boat

explanation.surface: A knight sets out on a sea journey that drags on slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is the proverbial example of a slow creature, crawling along at a famously sluggish pace.

clue.text: See 3
Indian musician has oil splashed on food

indicators.note: a splashed liquid is spattered about, so its letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: Ravi Shankar was the famous Indian sitar player
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A sitar player spills oil over his dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels with a filling, an Italian dish.

clue.text: See 3
Enthusiast hit something under the bonnet

blocks.note: a fan is an enthusiast
to belt is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A supporter strikes something, perhaps a hat, in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: The bonnet is the British word for a car's hood, so what is under it is engine equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan belt is the rubber drive belt in a car engine, sitting beneath the hood.

clue.text: See 3
Concealment when pair of leaders are lost in battle

indicators.text: when pair of leaders are lost
indicators.note: the first two letters, the word's leaders, are dropped from its front

blocks.note: secrecy is the keeping of things hidden

explanation.surface: A cover-up in which two commanders go missing in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Crécy was a 1346 battle of the Hundred Years' War, won by the English longbowmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Crecy names a famous fourteenth-century battlefield in northern France where Edward III defeated the French.

clue.text: What's offered with litre in hacienda, possibly?

definitions.text: What's offered with litre in hacienda, possibly?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the Spanish word for a ranch
possibly hints that a different arrangement of these letters is possible

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for litre
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks what dish might be served alongside a litre of something at a Mexican ranch house.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a dish you might well be served at a hacienda.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a rolled tortilla with a filling and sauce, Mexican fare offered at a ranch.
